text:
When my father ate

his lips became

greasy

with the food

and while he ate

he talked about how

good the food was

and how

most people

didn’t eat

as well

as we did.

He liked

to wipe up

what was left

on the plate

with a piece of

bread,

while making

noises of approval

that sounded more like

grunts

he slurped the

coffee,

making a loud

bubbling

noise

and then

set down

the cup.

‘What’s for dessert,

Jell-O?’


My mother

brought it

in a large dish

and my father

served it

and as it fell onto the plate

the Jell-O made

a strange noise,

almost like

the sound of a

fart.


Then came

the whipped cream,

heaps of it

on the Jell-O.

‘mmm, Jell-O and

whipped cream!’

my father sucked the

Jell-O and whipped cream

off the spoon.

It sounded as if

he were entering

a streamlined

tunnel.

After finishing

that

he wiped his mouth

with an enormous white napkin,

rubbing hard

in circular

motions,

the napkin

almost hid

his entire

face

and after that

he took out

the Camel

cigarettes.

He lit one

with a wooden

kitchen match,

and then left

the match

still burning

in an ashtray,

then a sip

of coffee,

he set down the cup again

and took a good drag

on the Camel.

‘mmm, that meal

was good!’

Soon afterward

in my room,

lying on the bed

in the dark,

what I had

eaten

and what I had

seen

managed

to make me

sick.

The only

good thing

was

hearing

the crickets

outside.


Outside

in another world

where I

did not live.




‘Dinner,’ 1933

translation.title: Dinner 1933
translation.editorial_note:
Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The food sounds, brand name, closing source title, and supplied spacing are retained.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
